mainEntity.name: Should I use an AI website builder, WordPress, a traditional builder, or hire a developer?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Compare platforms by required features, ownership, exportability, integrations, editing experience, performance, accessibility controls, support, and total cost. Do not choose solely because a demo produces attractive pages from a prompt.

Context: Community discussions repeatedly raise the tradeoff between fast setup and platform lock-in, especially when exporting or deploying elsewhere is difficult. A simple site may benefit from an all-in-one platform, while a growing project may need greater control.

Key factors:
- Simple brochure site versus ecommerce or software
- Hosted convenience versus portability
- Built-in tools versus third-party connections
- Owner’s ability to maintain the site

Practical guidance: Build a small test project and attempt to edit content, connect a domain, create a form, export or back up the site, and recover from an error. Record what happens before paying long term.

Run My AI Business’s tool-comparison education can help readers make a fit-based decision rather than follow hype.
acceptedAnswer.description: Choose based on complexity and ownership needs. AI builders suit fast, simple launches; traditional systems may offer broader control; a professional is more appropriate for complex integrations or high-stakes requirements. Test editing, backups, and portability first.
